Fritzson, A. and Berntsson, T. (2006). Efficient energy use in a slaughter and meat processing plant - opportunities for process integration. Journal of Food Engineering 76(4), 594-604. doi:10.1016/j.jfoodeng.2005.06.007

Locators are printed journal pages 594-604 (PDF page = printed - 593). Pinch and shaftwork-targeting case study of a modern Swedish slaughter and meat processing plant; plant data are confidential and shown only as curves. Main file: the suggested new heat pump (about 1 MW, condenser 62 degC; R134a alternative COP about 6) and the single-stage compression/absorption heat pump (COP 5.3 at 65-70 degC, reprinted from Hulten & Berntsson 2002). _measures: refrigeration shaftwork savings (5%, >10%, 16% in a reference plant; EUR 40,500/yr), heat-exchange and heat-pump savings (30% of external heat demand in a less modern plant). Not loaded: composite-curve values (read from charts only). Traps: the 1 MW is a targeting estimate from average data; no costs other than the relative R134a saving and the annual electricity saving.
